newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuwait naphtha talks to start June 9 in London.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait naphtha talks to start June 9 in London.

text.p: Kuwait and its Asian naphtha customers will hold term talks from June 9 on one-year supply contracts starting in August, oil product traders said on Thursday.
About a dozen trading houses from Japan and South Korea are expected to exchange market views with Kuwait during the talks before setting the new price, they said.
Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) last June set the naphtha price for the current term year that started in August 1996 at $7.90 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes.
During the upcoming talks, to be held in London, KPC is expected to seek a premium of more than $13.50, traders said.

Earlier this year, when KPC negotiated with Asian customers for one-year contracts starting in March 1997, Kuwait was able to clinch a term price of $13.50 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes, due to growing petrochemical feedstock demand for naphtha in Asia.
Most one-year Asian supply contracts cover cargoes lifted in the year beginning either in March or in August.
The current market environment is not so favourable for KPC, however, given ample near-term supplies in Asia, traders said.

"Kuwait is likely to come to the talks with firm intentions of a substantial price hike, but demands for an extraordinary price increase will not be easily accepted," one Japanese naphtha trader said.
Japan and South Korea are expected to import about two million tonnes of naphtha from KPC during the term year starting in August, traders added.
